description: Hand-labelled replies for measuring classification accuracy. Written to resemble real cold-outreach responses: hedged, polite, and often carrying a soft no inside an agreeable opener. Deliberately includes cases where the surface sentiment and the actual intent disagree.

examples.text: Sounds interesting - can you do Tuesday afternoon? Happy to jump on a quick call.
examples.label: interested
examples.note: Explicit agreement plus a proposed time.

examples.text: Thanks for reaching out. Could you send over some more detail on how the forecasting works and what the pricing looks like?
examples.label: needs_info
examples.note: Open, but wants material before committing to a conversation.

examples.text: We're mid-season right now so this isn't a priority. Worth picking up again after our Q1 planning cycle.
examples.label: not_now
examples.note: Not a refusal - a deferral with a stated timeframe.

examples.text: I don't handle inventory planning any more. Priya in our supply chain team would be the right person - I can forward this on.
examples.label: wrong_person

examples.text: Please remove me from your list and do not contact me again.
examples.label: unsubscribe

examples.text: Appreciate the note but we already use an in-house forecasting model, so no need for anything here. Thanks anyway.
examples.label: not_now
examples.note: Hard case: polite, and declines this approach rather than all contact. A classifier that reads 'no need' as an opt-out fails here.

examples.text: Interesting timing - we've been struggling with markdowns this season. What would onboarding actually involve?
examples.label: needs_info
examples.note: Hard case: states a real pain point and sounds warm, but the ask is for information, not a meeting.

examples.text: Not something I'm across - try our procurement team at the head office.
examples.label: wrong_person
examples.note: Hard case: terse, reads dismissive, but is a redirect rather than a refusal.
